context.analysis:
## Overview
[The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system processes card-not-present authorizations for a mid-size payment processor to detect fraud in real time while providing a secure case management interface for analysts. It operates within AWS eu-west-1 under strict PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance, maintaining high availability and a 7-year immutable audit trail.]

## Key Elements
* Payment Processor Systems (External API Consumer)
* Fraud Analyst & Risk/Compliance Officer (Internal Users)
* Identity Provider (AWS IAM / OIDC)
* Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening Software System (AWS ECS/Lambda, DynamoDB, Kafka)
* Model Registry / Feature Store (AWS SageMaker / S3 with AWS Signer)
* Immutable Audit Storage (AWS S3 Object Lock with AWS KMS CMK)

## Relationships
* Payment Processor Systems -> Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening System: HTTPS / gRPC (Synchronous authorization scoring at 3,000 TPS)
* Fraud Analysts -> Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening System: HTTPS (Secure browser access for case management and review)
* Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening System -> Model Registry: HTTPS / S3 API (Zero-downtime dynamic rule and model fetching)
* Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening System -> Immutable Audit Storage: AWS SDK / S3 API (WORM-compliant decision logging)
* Users -> Identity Provider: HTTPS / OpenID Connect (Enterprise SSO and hardware-token MFA)

## Technology Stack
* AWS ECS / Lambda: Container and serverless compute chosen for cost efficiency within the €25k monthly budget and operational simplicity for a 3-person team.
* AWS DynamoDB & Kafka: Low-latency data storage and event streaming to maintain <50ms P99 decision latency.
* AWS SageMaker & S3: Machine learning and feature store infrastructure enabling zero-downtime model and rule updates.
* AWS S3 Object Lock & KMS: Tamper-evident, WORM-compliant storage meeting the 7-year regulatory audit mandate.
* AWS Signer: Cryptographic code-signing for dynamic model artifacts to prevent supply-chain poisoning.

## Rationale
[This architecture satisfies strict PCI-DSS Level 1 security and 7-year auditability requirements using robust AWS managed services while staying within a 25,000 EUR monthly budget. It leverages a 3-person engineering team efficiently through serverless and managed components, and ensures resilient, low-latency performance via fail-open integration policies.]

containers.analysis:
## Overview
Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system screens card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud and manages analyst reviews. It operates within AWS eu-west-1 to process payments securely while maintaining compliance and auditability.

## Key Elements
* Fraud Analysts and Merchant Risk Managers
* AWS API Gateway / Envoy (Ingestion)
* Scoring Engine Container (Go/Rust on AWS ECS Fargate)
* Case Management Backend (Node.js/Python on ECS Fargate)
* Case Management UI (React on AWS S3 + CloudFront)
* Rule & Model Distribution Service (AWS SQS + S3)
* Audit Writer Sidecar / Async Worker (Go/Lambda)
* Amazon ElastiCache (Redis Feature Store)
* AWS QLDB / S3 Object Lock (Immutable Audit Storage)
* AWS Secrets Manager and AWS App Mesh

## Relationships
* Payment Processor to AWS API Gateway via HTTPS/gRPC
* Scoring Engine to ElastiCache via VPC peering for feature lookups
* Scoring Engine to Audit Storage via Amazon SQS for asynchronous event streaming
* Control Plane to Scoring Engine via gRPC/S3 for zero-downtime config updates
* Case Management UI to Case Management Backend via HTTPS/REST

## Technology Stack
* AWS ECS Fargate: Container orchestration chosen for low operational overhead matching the 3-engineer team constraint.
* Go or Rust: Selected for the Scoring Engine to guarantee sub-50ms P99 decision latency.
* AWS QLDB / S3 Object Lock: Provides tamper-evident storage to satisfy 7-year auditability requirements.
* React on AWS S3 and CloudFront: Delivers zero-infrastructure-overhead frontend for case management.
* Amazon ElastiCache (Redis): Enables low-latency in-memory feature lookups.

## Rationale
This architecture uses managed AWS services to minimize operational burden for a three-engineer team while respecting the 25,000 EUR monthly budget constraint. It separates high-throughput synchronous scoring from asynchronous auditing to meet stringent sub-50ms latency and PCI-DSS compliance requirements.

AWS API Gateway / Envoy.analysis:
## Overview
The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system screens card-not-present payment authorizations for a mid-size payment processor and manages analyst reviews. It provides automated scoring, case management, and strict compliance enforcement within AWS.

## Key Elements
- AWS API Gateway / Envoy (Ingestion Layer)
- Scoring Engine Container (Go/Rust on AWS ECS Fargate)
- Case Management Backend (Node.js/Python on ECS Fargate)
- Case Management UI (React on AWS S3 + CloudFront)
- Amazon ElastiCache (Redis Feature Store)
- AWS QLDB / S3 Object Lock (Immutable Audit Storage)

## Relationships
- Payment Processor Systems -> AWS API Gateway / Envoy: Sends payment authorizations for screening [HTTPS/gRPC]
- AWS API Gateway / Envoy -> Scoring Engine Container: Routes scoring requests [gRPC over internal VPC mTLS]
- Scoring Engine Container -> Amazon ElastiCache: Retrieves features [Redis Protocol]
- Scoring Engine Container -> AWS QLDB / S3 Object Lock: Stores audit decisions [AWS SDK / HTTPS]

## Technology Stack
- AWS API Gateway / Envoy: Handles high-throughput secure edge routing and Wasm tokenization.
- AWS ECS Fargate: Runs backend services with serverless container orchestration to meet budget limits.
- Amazon ElastiCache (Redis): Provides low-latency feature lookups for sub-50ms P99 performance.
- AWS QLDB / S3 Object Lock: Ensures tamper-evident, 7-year regulatory auditability.

## Rationale
This architecture uses serverless and managed AWS services to meet the strict 25,000 EUR monthly budget constraint while supporting 3,000 requests per second. Decoupled ECS containers and robust edge routing ensure PCI-DSS compliance and high availability.

Scoring Engine Container.analysis:
## Overview
The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system evaluates card-not-present payment authorizations to detect fraud and manage analyst reviews. It operates within AWS eu-west-1, ensuring PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance, sub-50ms P99 latency, and tamper-evident 7-year auditability.

## Key Elements
* Fraud Analysts & Compliance Officers (Users)
* Payment Processors & Merchants (External Systems)
* AWS API Gateway / Envoy
* Scoring Engine Container (Rust on AWS ECS Fargate)
* Amazon ElastiCache (Redis Feature Store)
* Immutable Audit Storage (AWS QLDB / S3 Object Lock)
* Rule & Model Distribution Service (AWS SQS + S3)
* AWS Secrets Manager

## Relationships
* AWS API Gateway / Envoy -> Scoring Engine Container: Forwards payment authorization requests [mTLS / HTTP/2]
* Scoring Engine Container -> Amazon ElastiCache: Fetches real-time transaction features [TLS-encrypted TCP/Redis]
* Rule & Model Distribution Service -> Scoring Engine Container: Supplies cryptographically verified Wasm rules [gRPC/S3]
* Scoring Engine Container -> Immutable Audit Storage: Flushes signed decision and explainability payloads asynchronously [HTTPS/REST]

## Technology Stack
* Rust: Chosen for the Scoring Engine Container to guarantee deterministic memory usage and sub-50ms P99 latency.
* AWS ECS Fargate: Provides isolated, managed container execution with strict runtime hardening (read-only root filesystem, dropped capabilities).
* Amazon ElastiCache (Redis): Delivers ultra-low latency feature retrieval over TLS-encrypted connections.
* WebAssembly (Wasm): Enables zero-downtime rule and scoring model updates with cryptographic signature verification.
* AWS Secrets Manager: Secures cryptographic keys for Wasm validation and audit signing via IAM task roles.

## Rationale
This architecture uses memory-safe Rust running on AWS ECS Fargate to reliably process 3,000 TPS under 50ms without garbage collection pauses. Enforcing mTLS, Wasm signature verification, and immutable audit logging satisfies strict PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and 7-year auditability within a 3-engineer team and 25,000 EUR monthly budget.

Case Management Backend.analysis:
## Overview
The Case Management Backend provides secure, scalable case administration and review workflows for fraud analysts within the Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system. It processes suspicious transactions while strictly enforcing PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and 7-year tamper-evident auditability.

## Key Elements
- Case Management Backend: NestJS (TypeScript) container running on AWS ECS Fargate
- API Router / Controller: Handles REST requests and JWT validation
- Case Service: Implements case lifecycle logic, bulk actions, and SLA-based routing
- SLA Worker / Scheduler Component: Manages background timers and auto-escalations via `@nestjs/schedule`
- Audit Logger Component: Records cryptographically signed analyst actions
- Data Access Layer: Utilizes an ORM to manage relational data
- Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL: Managed relational database with AES-256 encryption
- Immutable Audit Storage: Secure target for tamper-evident audit logs

## Relationships
- Case Management UI -> API Router / Controller: Sends API requests for case operations [HTTPS/REST, TLS 1.3]
- API Router / Controller -> Identity Provider: Validates JWTs and enforces RBAC [HTTPS/REST]
- Case Service -> Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL: Reads and writes case state and search indexes [TCP/TLS, Port 5432]
- Audit Logger Component -> Immutable Audit Storage: Writes signed analyst action logs [HTTPS/REST]

## Technology Stack
- TypeScript & NestJS: Chosen for structured modularity and high developer velocity
- Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL: Selected for relational ACID guarantees and built-in search indexing without operational complexity
- AWS ECS Fargate: Provides container orchestration within a 3-engineer constraint
- AWS KMS: Implements AES-256 encryption and key rotation for data protection

## Rationale
This architecture balances robust security and strict compliance requirements with rapid developer velocity for a small team. The serverless container and managed database approach fits within the fixed budget while supporting sub-minute failover and long-term auditability.

Case Management UI.analysis:
## Overview
React-based single-page application hosted on AWS S3 and distributed via CloudFront for fraud case review. Enables analysts to process suspended payments securely while strictly enforcing PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance.

## Key Elements
- Case Management UI Container (React on AWS S3 + CloudFront)
- Routing & Auth Controller Component (React Router)
- Case Workspace Component (React / TanStack Table)
- Audit & Explainability View Component (D3.js / Tailwind CSS)
- Queue Analytics & Filtering Engine Component (React Context / Zustand)
- External Identity Provider & Case Management Backend

## Relationships
- Fraud Analysts -> Case Management UI: Accesses secure case management interface [HTTPS]
- Routing & Auth Controller -> Identity Provider: Validates OIDC/JWT session tokens [HTTPS]
- Case Workspace Component & Audit & Explainability View -> Case Management Backend: Sends API requests for operations and data [HTTPS/REST JSON]
- Case Workspace Component -> Queue Analytics & Filtering Engine: Queries client-side risk queues [In-memory]

## Technology Stack
- React: Provides a modern, component-based UI framework.
- AWS S3 + CloudFront: Delivers zero-infrastructure-overhead static hosting supporting the 3-engineer team constraint and 25,000 EUR monthly budget.
- React Router: Handles client-side routing and OIDC/JWT session validation.
- React / TanStack Table: Renders high-performance risk queues and case workspaces.
- D3.js / Tailwind CSS: Visualizes model explainability data and feature attributions.
- React Context / Zustand: Manages client-side queue sorting, SLA timers, and risk prioritization state.

## Rationale
This architecture leverages serverless static hosting to eliminate infrastructure maintenance overhead for a three-engineer team while keeping costs within the 25,000 EUR monthly budget. Furthermore, strict client-side isolation ensures full card numbers never reach the browser, satisfying PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance requirements.

[The system is a real-time payment fraud screening platform that evaluates payment authorizations and manages suspicious cases. Its core purpose is to screen card-not-present transactions for fraud within strict latency limits while supporting auditability.]

Audit Writer Sidecar / Async Worker.analysis:
## Overview
Real-time payment fraud screening system for card-not-present transactions, ensuring sub-50ms decisions and 7-year tamper-evident auditability. Operated by 3 engineers on AWS under a €25,000/month budget with PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance.

## Key Elements
- **Users**: Fraud Analyst, Risk/Compliance Officer
- **External Systems**: Payment Processor Systems, Identity Provider, Model Registry / Feature Store, Immutable Audit Storage (AWS QLDB / S3 Object Lock)
- **Containers**: AWS API Gateway / Envoy, Scoring Engine Container (Go/Rust, AWS ECS Fargate), Case Management Backend (Node.js/Python, ECS Fargate), Case Management UI (React, AWS S3 + CloudFront), Rule & Model Distribution Service (AWS SQS + S3), Audit Writer Sidecar (Go, ECS Fargate), Amazon ElastiCache (Redis)
- **Components (Audit Writer Sidecar)**: Audit Event Consumer, Tamper-Evident Formatter & Signer (Ed25519/AWS KMS), Immutable Storage Client, DLQ & Metric Forwarder, Local Ring Buffer & Persistence Manager (`mmap`)

## Relationships
- **Scoring Engine** ➔ *(Local IPC / UNIX Domain Socket)* ➔ **Audit Event Consumer** (High-throughput, low-latency)
- **Tamper-Evident Formatter** ➔ *(AWS KMS SDK)* ➔ **AWS KMS** (Envelope encryption)
- **Immutable Storage Client** ➔ *(HTTPS / TLS 1.3)* ➔ **AWS QLDB / S3 Object Lock** (Write-once, append-only)
- **DLQ & Metric Forwarder** ➔ *(AWS SDK)* ➔ **Amazon SQS / CloudWatch**
- **Client UI** ➔ *(HTTPS / TLS 1.3)* ➔ **AWS API Gateway / Envoy**

## Technology Stack
- **AWS ECS Fargate**: Low-maintenance serverless container orchestration fitting the 3-engineer team constraint
- **Go / Rust**: High-performance languages ensuring strict P99 latency < 50ms at 3,000 TPS
- **Amazon ElastiCache (Redis)**: Low-latency feature store for real-time scoring inputs
- **AWS QLDB / S3 Object Lock**: Tamper-evident, append-only storage guaranteeing 7-year regulatory auditability
- **Ed25519 & AWS KMS**: Cryptographic signing and envelope encryption ensuring data security and PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance

## Rationale
Decoupling asynchronous audit logging via a sidecar pattern protects the critical 50ms scoring SLA while guaranteeing strict tamper-evident compliance. Managed AWS services minimize operational overhead for a three-engineer team within a fixed €25,000 monthly budget.

Amazon ElastiCache.analysis:
## Overview
The system screens card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud in real-time while providing case management for fraud analysts. It ensures sub-50ms decision latency and compliance with PCI-DSS Level 1 within a strict AWS budget.

## Key Elements
* Amazon ElastiCache (Redis Cluster): In-memory feature store for low-latency lookups.
* Scoring Engine Container: Go/Rust service running on AWS ECS Fargate.
* Model Registry / Feature Store: External system supplying scoring models and features.
* AWS CloudWatch & SNS: Monitoring and alerting infrastructure.
* AWS Secrets Manager: Credential management for Redis AUTH tokens.

## Relationships
* Scoring Engine Container -> Amazon ElastiCache: Performs feature lookups via TCP/Redis with TLS 1.3 and Redis AUTH tokens.
* Model Registry / Feature Store -> Amazon ElastiCache: Synchronizes features via asynchronous worker over TCP/Redis.
* Amazon ElastiCache -> AWS CloudWatch: Emits performance metrics and slow logs.

## Technology Stack
* AWS ElastiCache (Redis OSS, `cache.m6g.large` nodes): Chosen for sub-millisecond retrieval speeds to meet P99 latency requirements.
* Redis `volatile-lru` eviction policy: Prevents memory bloat and controls infrastructure costs.
* TLS 1.3 and Redis AUTH: Enforces strict data-in-transit security for PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance.
* AWS KMS: Encrypts data at rest within the cache cluster.

## Rationale
This architecture uses an in-memory Redis cluster to achieve sub-millisecond feature lookups, guaranteeing decision latencies below 50ms at scale. Stringent security controls and budget-conscious node sizing satisfy PCI-DSS Level 1 mandates and financial constraints without exceeding operational capacity.

AWS QLDB / S3 Object Lock.analysis:
## Overview
The Immutable Audit Storage container uses Amazon QLDB and Amazon S3 Object Lock to ensure every payment fraud screening decision is cryptographically verifiable and retained securely. It guarantees PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and a 7-year audit trail while maintaining cost efficiency for a small engineering team.

## Key Elements
- **Audit Ingestion Service**: AWS Lambda written in Go, receiving batched decision logs.
- **QLDB Journal Ledger**: Amazon QLDB storing structured decision metadata, model versions, and cryptographic inclusion proofs.
- **S3 Compliance Vault**: Amazon S3 with Object Lock (Compliance Mode) storing raw payload inputs.
- **AWS KMS**: Manages Customer Managed Keys (CMKs) for data encryption at rest.
- **Risk & Compliance Officers / Fraud Analysts**: External personas accessing audit logs and compliance reports.

## Relationships
- **Audit Writer Sidecar** -> **Audit Ingestion Service**: Sends batched decision logs via `Amazon SQS` and `AWS SDK (HTTPS)`.
- **Audit Ingestion Service** -> **QLDB Journal Ledger**: Stores structured journal entries using `QLDB Driver (DQL/PartiQL)`.
- **Audit Ingestion Service** -> **S3 Compliance Vault**: Stores raw payloads using `AWS SDK (HTTPS)` over `AWS PrivateLink`.
- **Audit Ingestion Service** -> **AWS KMS**: Encrypts and decrypts data via `AWS SDK (HTTPS)`.
- **Auditor / Compliance Officer** -> **QLDB / S3 Vault**: Executes cryptographic verification via `AWS Console / AWS SDK (HTTPS)`.

## Technology Stack
- **Amazon QLDB**: Chosen for immutable, cryptographically verifiable transaction metadata.
- **Amazon S3 Object Lock (Compliance Mode)**: Chosen to enforce Write-Once-Read-Many (WORM) storage for raw payloads.
- **AWS Lambda (Go)**: Chosen for serverless, low-overhead event processing managed by three engineers.
- **AWS KMS**: Chosen for encryption at rest using Customer Managed Keys with annual key rotation.
- **S3 Glacier / Lifecycle Rules**: Chosen to transition data to deep archival tiers to remain under the 25,000 EUR monthly budget.

## Rationale
This architecture uses serverless managed AWS services to minimize operational overhead for a three-engineer team while strictly satisfying PCI-DSS Level 1 and 7-year auditability mandates (R-06). Cost constraints are respected through automated S3 Glacier lifecycle transitions.
